content_voiceover: This slide maps out the therapeutic landscape for AIHA, and while boards won't expect encyclopedic drug knowledge, they will expect you to know first-line therapy and the general concept of where newer agents act. First-line for warm AIHA remains corticosteroids, with IVIG and splenectomy as classic second-line options, since warm AIHA is driven by extravascular destruction in the spleen via Fc-receptor-mediated phagocytosis, splenectomy makes physiologic sense. Beyond that, the pathway breaks into several targetable nodes worth recognizing by category rather than memorizing every name. B-cell directed therapy, rituximab, an anti-CD20 antibody, is the classic steroid-sparing, second-line agent you should know cold, alongside newer agents like ibrutinib, a BTK inhibitor, and BAFF inhibitors. Plasma-cell directed therapy targets the antibody-producing cells directly, bortezomib and daratumumab. Complement inhibition is a major growing category, sutimlimab targets C1 and is FDA-approved specifically for cold agglutinin disease, since cold AIHA is complement-driven, while eculizumab targets C5, more familiar from PNH. FcRn blockers like nipocalimab are a newer mechanism, they accelerate degradation of circulating IgG antibody. And supportive measures matter too, folate supplementation for the chronic hemolysis, and EPO or luspatercept to support marrow compensation. The big picture for boards, warm AIHA equals steroids plus splenectomy plus rituximab, cold agglutinin disease equals complement inhibition with sutimlimab.
keypoints: First-line warm AIHA: corticosteroids; second-line: rituximab (anti-CD20), IVIG, splenectomy
Complement inhibitors: sutimlimab (C1) FDA-approved for cold agglutinin disease; eculizumab (C5)
Plasma-cell/B-cell directed agents: bortezomib, daratumumab, ibrutinib, BAFF inhibitors
FcRn blockers (e.g., nipocalimab) accelerate clearance of circulating IgG
Splenectomy targets extravascular (spleen/ADCC) clearance in warm AIHA
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, anchor on first-line therapy. Warm AIHA is treated with corticosteroids first, then rituximab, IVIG, or splenectomy as steroid-sparing or refractory options, splenectomy works because warm AIHA destruction happens mainly in the spleen. Cold agglutinin disease is complement-driven, so sutimlimab, a C1 inhibitor, is now FDA-approved specifically for it, while eculizumab blocks C5. Other categories to recognize by class include B-cell and plasma-cell directed agents like ibrutinib and daratumumab, and newer FcRn blockers that speed up clearance of pathogenic IgG. Don't forget supportive care, folate and agents that boost marrow compensation.
